I’ve never been easy with stillness. Even as a kid, I’d fidget, get called out for blurting things in class, stepping into other folk’s business. Now, if I see a supply boat, I’m the first to call out, maybe cut the radio check short, jump in mid-sentence. But is that me, or is it… something else talking through me? I’ve been feeling wound up lately—like I can’t sit still, even during dinner or when my wife and I are watching the evening news. The doctors said I should rest, but I find myself getting up, walking around the house for no real reason, fixing things that don’t need fixing. My wife says I’ve always been a bit restless, but it’s worse now. I hate waiting—at appointments, in line at the pharmacy—my chest gets tight, and I’ll just blurt out something before thinking.  

Lately, though... there are moments when I hear my name called when no one’s there, or I catch shadows moving in the corner of my eye. I don’t know if it’s real or just my mind playing tricks. It started maybe a few months back, around the same time the restlessness got worse. I used to be patient—worked a desk job for thirty years, you learn to sit and wait. But now, it’s like I’m being pushed by something inside.  

I can’t tell if the noise in my head came first, or the need to keep moving. Sometimes I wonder if people are watching me, but I can’t be sure. My wife says I’m just stressed, but it feels bigger than that.
